\begin{theorem}[Encoding a fan-in-two circuit as 3-SAT]
\lean{Complexity.TQBFHard.dagCktSatToSAT3_encode}
\label{Complexity.TQBFHard.dagCktSatToSAT3_encode}
\leanok
\uses{BoolCircuit.DAGCircuit, BoolCircuit.DAGCircuit.IsFaninTwo, BoolCircuit.DAGCircuit.decode_encode, BoolCircuit.DAGCircuit.encode, BoolCircuit.DAGCircuit.toCNF, BoolCircuit.dagCktSatToCNF, BoolCircuit.dagCktSatToSAT3, Std.Sat.CNF.serialize}
\difficulty{1}
Let $C$ be a well-formed acyclic Boolean circuit in which each gate has at most two
inputs. Applying the circuit-to-3-SAT transformation to the encoding of $C$ yields
exactly the binary serialization of the CNF formula formed from the circuit's Tseitin
clauses together with the clause asserting that its output is true.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Reduction width]
\lean{Complexity.TQBFHard.redW}
\label{Complexity.TQBFHard.redW}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.TQBFHard.vwid, Complexity.TQBFHard.wCoef}
For a nondeterministic Turing machine $N$ with Boolean symbols and natural numbers
$d,c$, define the width at input length $n$ to be $vwid(wCoef(N,d),c+1,n)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Reduction size]
\lean{Complexity.TQBFHard.redM}
\label{Complexity.TQBFHard.redM}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.TQBFHard.redW}
For a nondeterministic Turing machine $N$ with Boolean symbols and natural numbers
$d,c$, define the size at input length $n$ to be $3w^2+3w$, where
$w=vwid(wCoef(N,d),c+1,n)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Reduction exponent]
\lean{Complexity.TQBFHard.redK}
\label{Complexity.TQBFHard.redK}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.TQBFHard.wCoef}
For a nondeterministic Turing machine $N$ with Boolean symbols and a natural number $d$,
define the reduction exponent to be $3wCoef(N,d)^2+3wCoef(N,d)+3$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Reduction time bound]
\lean{Complexity.TQBFHard.redT}
\label{Complexity.TQBFHard.redT}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.TQBFHard.redK}
For a nondeterministic Turing machine $N$ with Boolean symbols, natural numbers $d,c$, a
deterministic Turing machine $V$ over Booleans, and natural numbers $CV,cV$, define the
time bound at input length $n$ to be
$CV\bigl(3wCoef(N,d)^2+3wCoef(N,d)+3\bigr)^{cV}(n+1)^{2(c+1)cV}+1$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Reduction circuit]
\lean{Complexity.TQBFHard.redCircuit}
\label{Complexity.TQBFHard.redCircuit}
\leanok
\uses{BoolCircuit.DAGCircuit, Complexity.TQBFHard.redM, Complexity.TQBFHard.redT, Complexity.cfgTab, Turing.pairEncode}
For a nondeterministic Turing machine $N$ with Boolean symbols, natural numbers $d,c$, a
deterministic Turing machine $V$ over Booleans, natural numbers $CV,cV$, and a finite
Boolean list $x$, define the reduction circuit on $x$ by applying the
configuration-table construction for $V$ with size parameter $3w^2+3w$ and time bound
$CV(3wCoef(N,d)^2+3wCoef(N,d)+3)^{cV}(|x|+1)^{2(c+1)cV}+1$ to the encoding of $x$ paired
with the empty list, where $w=vwid(wCoef(N,d),c+1,|x|)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Reduction quantifier prefix]
\lean{Complexity.TQBFHard.redQuants}
\label{Complexity.TQBFHard.redQuants}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.QBF.Quant, Complexity.TQBFHard.levelQuants, Complexity.TQBFHard.redW}
For a nondeterministic Turing machine $N$ with Boolean symbols, natural numbers $d,c$, a
deterministic Turing machine $V$ over Booleans, and natural numbers $CV,cV$, define the
quantifier prefix at length $n$ to be three consecutive blocks of $w$ existential
quantifiers followed by the level quantifier sequence with parameters $(w,w)$, where
$w=vwid(wCoef(N,d),c+1,n)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Reduction quantified Boolean formula]
\lean{Complexity.TQBFHard.redQBF}
\label{Complexity.TQBFHard.redQBF}
\leanok
\uses{BoolCircuit.DAGCircuit.toCNF, Complexity.QBF, Complexity.TQBFHard.redCircuit, Complexity.TQBFHard.redQuants, Std.Sat.CNF.serialize}
For a nondeterministic Turing machine $N$ with Boolean symbols, natural numbers $d,c$, a
deterministic Turing machine $V$ over Booleans, and natural numbers $CV,cV$, define the
quantified Boolean formula associated to a Boolean list $x$ to have quantifier prefix
given by the reduction quantifiers at length $|x|$, followed by one existential
quantifier for each serialized clause in the conjunctive normal form of the reduction
circuit on $x$; its matrix is that conjunctive normal form.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Reduction encoding map]
\lean{Complexity.TQBFHard.redMap}
\label{Complexity.TQBFHard.redMap}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.QBF.encode, Complexity.TQBFHard.redQBF}
For a nondeterministic Turing machine $N$ with Boolean symbols, natural numbers $d,c$, a
deterministic Turing machine $V$ over Booleans, and natural numbers $CV,cV$, define the
reduction map on a Boolean list $x$ to be the Boolean-list encoding of the quantified
Boolean formula associated to $x$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Length of the Reduction Quantifier List]
\lean{Complexity.TQBFHard.length_redQuants}
\label{Complexity.TQBFHard.length_redQuants}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.TQBFHard.length_levelQuants, Complexity.TQBFHard.redM, Complexity.TQBFHard.redQuants}
\difficulty{3}
For any natural number $n$, the list of quantifiers formed by concatenating three blocks
of existential quantifiers, each of length $R$, with the quantifier list for $R$ levels
and width $R$ has length $3R^2+3R$, where $R=A(c+1)(n+1)^a$ and $A,a,c$ are the
parameters defined by the reduction construction.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Reduction time bound]
\lean{Complexity.TQBFHard.time_le}
\label{Complexity.TQBFHard.time_le}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.TQBFHard.redK, Complexity.TQBFHard.redM, Complexity.TQBFHard.redT, Complexity.TQBFHard.redW, Complexity.TQBFHard.vwid, Complexity.TQBFHard.wCoef, Turing.length_pairEncode, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{5}
Let $N,d,c,V,CV,c_V$ be the machine and natural-number parameters in the definitions of
the reduction bounds, and let $x,\sigma$ be Boolean strings such that the length of
$\sigma$ is the reduction's output-width bound at input length $|x|$. Then
$CV\bigl((|\langle x,\sigma\rangle|+1)^{c_V}\bigr)$ is at most the reduction's time
bound at input length $|x|$, where $\langle x,\sigma\rangle$ is the specified pairing
encoding.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Evaluation of the reduction circuit]
\lean{Complexity.TQBFHard.eval_redCircuit}
\label{Complexity.TQBFHard.eval_redCircuit}
\leanok
\uses{BoolCircuit.DAGCircuit.eval, Complexity.TQBFHard.predB, Complexity.TQBFHard.redCircuit, Complexity.TQBFHard.redM, Complexity.TQBFHard.time_le, Complexity.TQBFHard.wCoef, Complexity.cfgTab_eval, Complexity.decide_emits_eq_of_computesInTime, Turing.FinTM.ComputesFunInTime, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime.mono, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{4}
Let $N$ be a nondeterministic Turing machine, let $d,c,C_V,c_V$ be natural numbers, and
let $V$ be a deterministic Turing machine that, on every bit string $y$, halts within
$C_V(|y|+1)^{c_V}$ steps and outputs the one-bit string whose bit is the predicate
$P(y)=\mathrm{predB}(N,d,c,w,d_c,y)$, where $w=4dW+W+12kd+3k+2|Q|+8$, $W=|H|+3k+1$,
$H=Q\times\{0,1,2\}$, and $d_c=c+1$. For every bit string $x$ and every Boolean sequence
$\tau$, the circuit with $\mathrm{redM}(N,d,c,|x|)$ input bits produced from $x$
evaluates on the initial segment of $\tau$ to $P(\langle
x,\tau_{<\mathrm{redM}(N,d,c,|x|)}\rangle)$, where the segment is encoded as a finite
bit string.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Truth of the Reduction Formula]
\lean{Complexity.TQBFHard.truth_redQBF}
\label{Complexity.TQBFHard.truth_redQBF}
\leanok
\uses{BoolCircuit.DAGCircuit.eval, BoolCircuit.DAGCircuit.toCNF, Complexity.QBF.prefixTruth_congr, Complexity.QBF.truth, Complexity.QBF.truth_exSuffix_of_pointwise, Complexity.TQBFHard.blockAcc, Complexity.TQBFHard.blockInit, Complexity.TQBFHard.blockStep, Complexity.TQBFHard.configBound_le_two_pow, Complexity.TQBFHard.eval_redCircuit, Complexity.TQBFHard.length_redQuants, Complexity.TQBFHard.levelMatrix, Complexity.TQBFHard.levelMatrix_iff_flat, Complexity.TQBFHard.mem_iff_mid, Complexity.TQBFHard.numVars_le_length_serialize, Complexity.TQBFHard.predB, Complexity.TQBFHard.predB_iff, Complexity.TQBFHard.prefixTruth_top, Complexity.TQBFHard.readBlock, Complexity.TQBFHard.redCircuit, Complexity.TQBFHard.redQBF, Complexity.TQBFHard.redQuants, Complexity.TQBFHard.redW, Complexity.TQBFHard.toCNF_extension_iff, Complexity.TQBFHard.uRec, Complexity.TQBFHard.vRec, Complexity.TQBFHard.vlen, Complexity.TQBFHard.vlen_le_vwid, Complexity.TQBFHard.vrad, Complexity.TQBFHard.wCoef, Complexity.cfgTab_isFaninTwo, Turing.FinNDTM.DecidesInSpace, Turing.FinTM.ComputesFunInTime}
\difficulty{6}
Let $N$ be a finite-state nondeterministic Turing machine that decides a language $L$
using space at most $d(n^c+1)$ on every input of length $n$. Let $V$ be a finite-state
deterministic Turing machine that, on every Boolean string $y$, outputs the one-bit
string whose bit is the predicate defined by the machine $N$ and parameters $d,c$
evaluated at $y$, and halts within $CV(|y|+1)^{c_V}$ steps. Then, for every Boolean
string $x$, the quantified Boolean formula $\rho(x)$ constructed from $N,d,c,V,CV,c_V$ is
true if and only if $x\in L$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Polynomial-time output of a prescribed unary length]
\lean{Complexity.TQBFHard.pt_redM}
\label{Complexity.TQBFHard.pt_redM}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.PolyTimeComputable, Complexity.PolyTimeComputable.append, Complexity.TQBFHard.redM, Complexity.TQBFHard.redW, Complexity.TQBFHard.vwid, Complexity.TQBFHard.wCoef, Complexity.polyTimeComputable_polyUnary}
\difficulty{4}
For every finite nondeterministic Turing machine $N$, all natural numbers $d,c$, and
every finite Turing machine $V$ over the binary alphabet with natural numbers $C_V,c_V$,
the function sending an input $x$ to the string of $3R(|x|)^2+3R(|x|)$ ones is
polynomial-time computable, where $R(n)=W(n)(n+1)^{c+1}$ and
$W(n)=4dW_N+W_N+12k_Nd+3k_N+2|Q_N|+8$, with $W_N=h_N+3k_N+1$ and $h_N$ the number of
possible head summaries of $N$.
\end{theorem}
